newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM urges parliament to pass new tax laws.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM urges parliament to pass new tax laws.

text.p: Ukraine Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko warned parliamentaty deputies that if they failed to pass tax reforms early in the new year, the economy would contract.
"If the tax laws are not accepted, GDP (gross domestic product) will fall four percent in 1997, and 3.8 percent in 1998," Lazarenko said on Thursday.
Lazarenko urged parliament to approve the 1997 draft budget, which includes the new tax laws, in mid-January or February.
If accepted the economy is forecast to experience modest growth in 1997, its first year of growth in the post-Soviet era.
The government handed parliament the proposed tax laws and the draft budget in November. Lazarenko said the budget could not realistically be implemented without new tax laws.
The prime minister said the laws would bring a significant portion of Ukraine's large shadow economy into the open.
The current tax regime has been blamed for forcing many businesses, which can pay more than 100 percent of profits in tax, into the shadow economy.
The new tax laws will lower tax rates by broadening the tax base.
Lazarenko also said Ukraine could no longer afford to pay the same social benefits paid to citizens in the Soviet era.
